summary: Full extraction of 19 stored Mauritius documents (EDB annual report 2020/21, EDB residency portal pages and property guidelines, Citizenship and Immigration Acts, Finance Acts 2015-2025, EDB Act consolidation 2026, Budget Speech 2018-19). Only the EDB annual report has statistics: 14 numbers added (projects approved under PDS/Smart City/IHS, permits grandfathered to 10 years, nationality shares of all active OP/RP holders, a 50,000-retiree target). The laws and pages yield 81 dated rule rows (investment minimums, turnover targets, permit validity, PRP conditions, transfer deadlines, duties) and 10 events. No document gives permits by nationality for the investor or retiree categories specifically, or any count of residence permits under the property schemes.

events.title: IRS and RES certificates abolished; PDS and Smart City Scheme created
events.description: The Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2015 deleted the IRS and RES certificates from the Investment Promotion Act and empowered the Minister to set up the Property Development Scheme and Smart City Scheme (and the Mauritian Diaspora Scheme). Existing IRS/RES certificates stay in force and applications pending on or before 22 March 2015 continue under the old rules; buyers from IRS/RES companies keep resident status while they hold the property. The residence provision in the Immigration Act was rewritten for PDS and Smart City buyers at USD 500,000 (separate event).

The same Act added two investor occupation-permit categories (USD 100,000 with high-technology equipment; USD 40,000 for innovative start-ups) and set the retiree transfer at USD 2,500 a month.

In scope: infographic (p. 11) and text on real estate (pp. 12-13): projects approved under PDS (10), Smart City (3), IHS (2) and NRP (6, not a residence route); 286 residential acquisition authorisations worth MUR 10.3 billion (already in data); 25 business-property authorisations (MUR 1.25 bn, not a residence route); 2021/22 budget measures on IRS/RES/PDS/IHS/G+2 (rules legislated in FA 2021, taken from that Act). Work and live section (pp. 31-33): 2020/21 changes (permit validity 3 to 10 years, investor minimum USD 100,000 to 50,000, PRP investment USD 500,000 to 375,000, already recorded from FA 2020); Table 4 active OP/RP holders 30 June 2021 (investor 918, retired 758 already in data; professional 4,347 and self-employed 431 and total 6,454 out of scope); 5,138 dependants and 427 PRP holders (already in data); Table 5 permits grandfathered to 10 years (investor 764, retired 668 added; self-employed 358 out of scope); Figure 9 nationalities of all active OP/RP holders (8 shares added, mixed categories); Figure 10 OPs issued by sector 2014-June 2021 (all OP categories, percent by sector, sector labels garbled and not investor-specific: not taken); Premium Visa 510 approved (tourist long-stay visa, out of scope). Mandate to attract 50,000 retirees (added as target). Rest: economy, trade, manufacturing, financial services, governance, EDB financial statements (no permit fee revenue).

EDB residency portal page on the investor occupation permit (USD 100,000): minimum investment, 10-year validity, USD 1,000 permit fee from 11 July 2022 and USD 50 application fee from 1 Dec 2025 (both already in data), turnover conditions (MUR 5 million from year 3, MUR 8 million a year from year 5 for renewal), 60-day transfer deadline, PRP after 5 years with MUR 15 million a year or MUR 75 million over 5 years, dependants' permits, document lists. No statistics. Undated page.

EDB residency portal page on the residence permit for retired non-citizens aged 50+: USD 2,000 a month or USD 24,000 a year, 10-year validity renewable, PRP after 5 consecutive years, USD 1,000 permit fee from 11 July 2022 (already in data), right to invest without employment, tax residence (183/270 days, general tax rule, not taken), dependants, document lists. No statistics. Undated page.

EDB residency portal page on G+2 apartments: residence permit for purchases of at least USD 375,000 (Immigration Act s. 5(1)(ga), Budget 2021/22), valid while the property is owned; non-citizens may buy G+2 apartments from MUR 6 million (purchase permission, no residence: noted, not taken). No statistics. Undated page.

EDB residency portal page on the Integrated Resort Scheme: USD 375,000 minimum for residence, types of property (serviced plots up to 1.25 A / 5,276 m2), rights of owners; a 'Projects under the IRS' heading whose list is not in the stored HTML (loaded dynamically); links to the IRS/RES/PDS guidelines and forms. No statistics. Undated page.

EDB guidelines (Nov 2024) for buyers of residential property under IRS/RES/PDS: eligible buyers, off-plan payment schedule (25/10/35/25/5%, civil-law rule, not taken), documents, MUR 25,000 processing fee (already in data; same fee for resale applications), payment in foreign currency (first USD 500,000 when a local loan is used), residence for property above USD 375,000 while held, serviced land (IRS plots from USD 350,000, max 0.5275 ha; PDS plots max 2,100 m2, one per non-citizen permit holder; build within 5 years), rental via the scheme company, resale with 30 days' notice, registration duty and land transfer tax table. Annex: blank residence permit and UID application forms (OCR checked, no numbers). No statistics.

Mauritius Citizenship (Amendment) Act 1995 (scanned gazette pages, read by OCR; the pages also carry the Constitution (Amendment) Act 1995 and the start of the Secondary Schools Trust Fund Act 1995, not in scope). In scope: s. 5 new s. 9(3), 2 years' residence instead of the normal requirement for a person who invested at least MUR 3 million (amount and event already in data; residence period added). Also: registration of spouses after 4 years' cohabitation, resumption of citizenship from 1 May 1995 (not investment routes). Commencement by Proclamation (s. 8): the existing launch event uses the assent date 23 Aug 1995.

Mauritius Citizenship (Amendment) Act 1999 (Act 34 of 1999, one page): replaces 'MUR 3,000,000' in s. 9(3) by 'USD 500,000 or such other sum as may be prescribed'. Passed 30 Nov 1999, assented 7 Dec 1999 (the Act's own short title says 1998). Amount and event already in data; nothing else in it.

Mauritius Citizenship Act consolidated text (to 2003): acquisition by registration and naturalisation, loss, dual nationality, regulations (fees may be prescribed, none stated), Commonwealth schedule, dual-nationality oath. In scope: s. 9(3) reduced residence (2 years) for investors, printed as 'not less than 5,000 US dollars' (likely an error for 500,000; both added as terms with notes), s. 9(4) renunciation. No figures on use.

Immigration Act 1970, consolidated to 2009 amendments. In scope: residence for IRS owners and RES buyers of at least USD 500,000 (s. 5(1)(g), already in data); residence for investors and retirees (s. 5(1)(h)); permanent residence after 3 years for investor and retiree permit holders, 10-year PRP (s. 5A); occupation permit (s. 9A) and retiree permit (s. 9B) from 1 Oct 2006 (event already in data): 3-year validity, 2-working-day decision with deemed approval, prescribed fee and bank guarantee (amounts not stated); PRP bank guarantee up to MUR 50,000 (s. 10A); loss of status when Board of Investment certifies criteria no longer met (ss. 6, 6A); exempted persons incl. investors under the Permanent Resident Scheme (s. 7(1)(k)). Rest: admission, prohibited immigrants, deportation, offences (not in scope). Terms added for validity, PRP eligibility, decision deadline, PRP validity and guarantee.

Immigration Act 2022, replacing the 1970 Act. In scope: residence status for buyers of IRS/RES/IHS/PDS/Smart City property and G+2 apartments at USD 375,000 (alone or as each co-buyer's share) (s. 8); retiree permit (s. 10); permanent residence, 20-year validity, USD 1,500 monthly income to switch to retiree PRP (s. 11); investor occupation permit 10 years, 5-working-day deemed approval, extension of 3-year permits valid on 1 Sep 2020 (s. 12); family occupation permit 10 years (s. 14); transitional saving for IRS/RES owners (s. 39); consequential amendments to the EDB Act, Citizenship Act (s. 9(4) replaced: event added), and Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act (residents may buy other residential property from USD 350,000: purchase permission, no new residence route, not taken). Fees and deposits only 'as prescribed' (deposit up to MUR 100,000 applies to work-permit holders, not taken). Rest: admission, temporary residence for spouses, removal, offences (not in scope). Terms added; the Act's own event (2022-07-27) already in data.

Budget Speech 2018-19 with annex of budget measures. In scope: paras 107-109 proposed EDB citizenship scheme (USD 1 million to a Mauritius Sovereign Fund, USD 100,000 per family member) and passport scheme (USD 500,000, USD 50,000 per passport) (event already in data; not legislated, so no programme terms recorded); para 111 package for foreign retirees (apartment purchase, customs exemption up to Rs 2 million: event added); annex C.15(a) occupation permit fee payable on approval rather than on application, C.27 Passports Act fee for passports to high-net-worth individuals (proposals, noted here). Para 110 Foreign Manpower Scheme (OP in 5 days, employer pays one month's salary: work route, not in scope). No programme statistics or revenue estimates. Rest: general economic, social, tax and sector measures.

Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2015 (53 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax, banking, customs and other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 23 Immigration Act (residence for PDS/Smart City buyers at USD 500,000, already in data; saving for IRS/RES owners; Diaspora PRP; non-citizen ID numbers and register), s. 31 Investment Promotion Act (IRS/RES certificates abolished, PDS/SCS certificates, schemes by regulation; pending IRS/RES applications up to 22 March 2015 saved: event added; Schedule Part I item 1B 'any other investor' project value over MUR 20 million: term added; BOI One-Stop Shop for projects over MUR 20 million), s. 39 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act (PDS/SCS/IHS replace RES; saving for IRS/RES purchases), s. 55 commencement. No figures on use. Land (Duties and Taxes) and Registration Duty amendments contain no IRS/RES-specific rates.

Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2017 (61 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax and other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 25 Immigration Act (IHS buyers get resident status: event added; occupation permit for start-up investors, s. 9A(1A)); s. 29 Investment Promotion Act Schedule Part I new items 1E (USD 100,000 incl. high-tech equipment, USD 25,000 transfer) and 1F (USD 40,000 start-ups, 20% R&D) (terms added) and item 6 retired non-citizen USD 2,500 at issue and monthly (already in data); s. 41 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act: retirees may acquire a lifetime right to live in a care home or similar unit outside smart cities (no amount); s. 61 commencement. Land duty and registration duty amendments have no scheme-specific rates. No statistics.

Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2020 (74 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax, customs, banking, other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 16 EDB Act (new First Schedule in Third Schedule: criteria for investors, start-ups, food processing, film studio, other investors, professionals, young professionals, self-employed, retirees; PRP criteria Part II and pre-1 Sep 2020 Part III); s. 27 Immigration Act (USD 375,000 property residence incl. IRS/RES/IHS/PDS/SCS, PRP direct investment USD 375,000, permits 10 years, PRP 20 years, transitional PRP s. 5A(5AB), right of retirees to invest s. 9H); s. 45 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) (Smart City serviced plots); s. 32 land duty references; s. 74 commencement (ss. 16(f) and 27 from 2 Sep 2020). Terms added for all investor and retiree criteria not already in data; professional and self-employed criteria (salaries, USD 35,000 self-employed) are not investment routes and were not taken. Two events added. Note: the existing FA 2020 terms and the property threshold event use 7 Aug 2020 (Act date) although s. 74(7) gives 2 Sep 2020.

Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2021 (97 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax, customs, finance and other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 22 EDB Act (registration and deregistration rules incl. revocation of permits, Premium Investor Scheme for projects of MUR 500 million (business incentive, not residence), saving for pre-2006 investors, new First Schedule in the Fifth Schedule: investor USD 50,000 options and renewal income, retiree USD 1,500 a month or USD 18,000 a year, PRP criteria (USD 375,000; 3 years plus MUR 15 million; retiree USD 54,000), pre-Sept 2020 and pre-Oct 2006 criteria, Family Occupation Permit USD 250,000 to the COVID-19 Projects Development Fund (already in data)); s. 37 Immigration Act (G+2 apartments USD 375,000 and FOP s. 9CA: already in data with launch event; permits deemed approved after 5 working days; PRP 20 years; retiree PRP conversion USD 1,500 a month). Restated amounts identical to the 2020 schedule were not added again; the 2020 'film studio' and 'any other investor' items were dropped (valid_to set on those 2020 terms). s. 77 Registration Duty Act and s. 44 Land (Duties and Taxes) Act change IRS/RES/IHS duty references and delete USD 50,000/25,000 minimum-duty alternatives without printing the scheme rates (not taken). s. 62 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act: EDB register of non-citizen property. Terms added: decision deadline, PRP conversion income, pre-2006 turnover, FOP validity.

Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2023 (93 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax, customs and other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 24 EDB Act (Premium Investor Scheme objects (business incentive); First Schedule: investor USD 50,000 with proof of funds and transfer within 60 days, high-tech option with USD 25,000 within 60 days (from 1 Aug 2023); retiree criteria replaced by bank statement showing USD 18,000 or guaranteed income USD 1,500 a month; professional and self-employed changes not in scope); s. 37 Immigration Act 2022 (Sustainable City Scheme added: event added; senior-living PDS property above USD 200,000 for over-50s, already in data). s. 93(18) says s. 37(b)(iii) (senior living) is deemed in operation from 27 April 2019, but the existing senior-living term and event are dated 20 Jul 2023: needs a decision. s. 59 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act: residents may buy one other residential property from USD 500,000 (was USD 350,000), and s. 70 Registration Duty Act s. 14A threshold raised from USD 350,000 to USD 500,000 (purchase permission and duty for existing residents, not a residence route: noted, not taken). Second Schedule passenger fees (USD 13-60) not in scope.

Finance Act 2025 (66 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax and other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 13 EDB Act new First Schedule (investor USD 50,000 and USD 100,000 options with year-1, cumulative year-5 and renewal turnover targets, 60-day transfer; start-ups; ProPass/Expert Pass and young professionals and self-employed USD 50,000 (not investment routes, not taken); Family Occupation Permit USD 250,000 (already in data); retiree USD 2,000 initial and USD 24,000 a year or USD 2,000 a month (already in data); PRP after 5 years: investor MUR 15 million a year or MUR 75 million, retiree USD 200,000 (already in data), professional MUR 400,000 salary, self-employed MUR 3 million); s. 25 Immigration Act 2022 (retiree permit 10 years, PRP 20 years, retiree conversion USD 40,000 a year, investor permit 10 years, Joint Committee and NELS procedure, dependants up to 24, combined work-residence permit, annual fee per foreign worker) commencing by Proclamation; s. 49 Registration Duty Act and s. 29 Land (Duties and Taxes) Act: new duty basis for non-citizen purchases of EDB scheme property from 1 July 2026 (registration duty rate not printed; land transfer tax 10% on non-citizen-to-non-citizen transfers: term added); s. 44 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act; s. 63 Smart City Regulations (smart city fee for developers, not buyers). Terms and three events added.

Economic Development Board Act 2017 consolidated to Act 13 of 2026. In scope: definitions (golden visa issued under the Passports Act on EDB recommendation; IRS, RES, IHS, PDS, SCS); registration and deregistration of permit holders (s. 13-14; family occupation permit no longer listed); AI City Scheme (expedited permits for certificate holders); Second Schedule list of schemes incl. Property Development, Smart City, Sustainable City, Invest Hotel; First Schedule: investor USD 100,000 with 60-day transfer, MUR 5 million turnover from year 3 and MUR 8 million from year 5 for renewal (terms added); PRP: investor 5 years with MUR 15 million a year or MUR 75 million (same as Finance Act 2025, not repeated), AI Founder investing USD 1 million (term added), retiree 5 years and USD 200,000 (already in data), golden visa holder investing USD 1 million (already in data, with event); retiree criteria USD 2,000 initial and USD 24,000 a year or USD 2,000 a month (same as Finance Act 2025, not repeated); professional (MUR 50,000), young professional, self-employed USD 50,000 (not investment routes). Rest: EDB governance, other business schemes, financial provisions, consequential amendments of 2017.
